Playbook.name: Windows — Malicious PowerShell: AMSI/ETW Bypass or Offensive Tooling - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A PowerShell script block (4104) contained AMSI/ETW bypass strings or offensive-tooling names - amsiInitFailed, AmsiScanBuffer, EtwEventWrite, sekurlsa, Invoke-Mimikatz, Rubeus, Invoke-BloodHound, etc. Triage question: is this malicious PowerShell (credential theft/AD attack/evasion), or a security tool/false match?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: AMSI/ETW bypass disables PowerShell's malware scanning; the tooling strings indicate credential theft and AD attacks - strong compromise signals.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Malicious PowerShell
Signal.Details: 4104 script block with AMSI/ETW-bypass or offensive-tool strings.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the PowerShell script block is malicious tooling/evasion or a benign match.

Step.name: The offending script-block content
Step.Purpose: Reading the actual script block confirms real offensive tooling vs a benign string match.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.powershell_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "4104" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL sb = TO_LOWER(powershell.file.script_block_text) | WHERE sb LIKE "*amsiinitfailed*" OR sb LIKE "*amsiscanbuffer*" OR sb LIKE "*etweventwrite*" OR sb LIKE "*sekurlsa*" OR sb LIKE "*invoke-mimikatz*" OR sb LIKE "*rubeus*" OR sb LIKE "*invoke-bloodhound*" OR sb LIKE "*invoke-kerberoast*" | KEEP @timestamp, user.name, powershell.file.script_block_text | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Read the script block: an actual AMSI-bypass one-liner or a mimikatz/Rubeus invocation is malicious. A security tool's detection signature or a defender's test script may match benignly - the content distinguishes them.

Step.name: What else did this host/account run around the script
Step.Purpose: Malicious PowerShell usually sits amid other attack activity (credential access, lateral movement).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4648","4672","5145") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY src | SORT c DESC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Explicit-credential logons (4648), remote logons or pipe access around the script support an active intrusion - escalate.

Node.Condition: The script block is genuine offensive tooling (mimikatz/Rubeus/BloodHound) or an AMSI/ETW bypass, especially amid other attack activity.
The match is a benign security-tool signature or a documented defender test.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PSMAL-SCRIPT, INV-02-PSMAL-CONTEXT to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A benign string match (security-tool signature, documented test).

Indicators.Item: Content is a detection signature/test, not an invocation.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the benign source; close as false_positive.

Indicators.Item: Real mimikatz/Rubeus/BloodHound invocation or AMSI bypass.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; open IR; treat host credentials as exposed.
Capture the full script; hunt the same tooling estate-wide.
Confirm with the security team; document; require deconfliction.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
